hints.content: The arrow points to all values greater than $-5$.
So, the inequality represents everything **greater than $-5$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**


[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at negative 5. A line running to the right starts at negative 5 and continues.

choices.clue:
The graph of $x >-4$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at negative 4. A line running to the right starts at negative 4 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/052d2a0ad7e0ed0ebced52ff22605478f0cdb0e0)

The graph of $x <5$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at 5. A line running to the left starts at 5 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/1727bf16edb8cdf3ef122cd01ecdc8b8bf975b52)

The graph of $x >5$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 1 to 9 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at 5. A line running to the right starts at 5 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/3d0bc20c60cf82b9459df5fb75f8a68a45696f2d)
